title: Creature
description: One bestiary creature — a HAZARD, not a villain (the bestiary design law). DERIVED from the authored content/packs/valley/bestiary.json roster (26 entries, CCODE-55 / SNG-250 §4) so generate('creature', ctx) validates against the same shape the hand-authored creatures have. `required` is the load-bearing core every authored entry carries and every consumer reads: bestiaryEncounters (random_encounters.js) turns each into a danger-gated encounter entry, noteBeastImage (app.js) renders it from `look`, and traditionMotivationsForGM (state.js) resolves a craft's DREAD by id. Authored entries also carry `clean` (how it dies), which no consumer reads today — deliberately NOT required here, so generation is not taught to fill a field the engine ignores.

id.description: stable slug; the roster key + the creatureId encounters and quest dreads refer to. An id-less creature is FILTERED OUT of the encounter pool entirely (random_encounters.js:59) — it would not exist.

name.description: what it is called in play — the encounter label and the image caption. Lowercase common-noun style like the authored roster ('glimmerlings', 'warpling hare'), not a proper name: it is a kind of thing, not a person.

tier.description: THE load-bearing field: it IS the fight's difficulty. BEAST_TIER maps it to the opponent's threat, the entry's weight, and its minDanger gate. An unknown value silently resolves to `notable`, so it must be one of these five: BEAST_TIER's own keys (random_encounters.js). SNG-658: the enum said `regional`, the rung renamed in SNG-599, which BEAST_TIER no longer knows, so a generated beast could be tiered into a silent `notable` — a creature tiered 'legendary' would fight as mid-tier without any error.

class.description: the bestiary grouping (e.g. manifested_creature, beast, precursor_construct) — rides on the encounter entry as creatureClass.

look.description: what it looks like — read by the beast-image prompt (art.js) and folded into the encounter seed the GM narrates from. Concrete and visual; this is the only description the art has to work with.

danger.description: what it DOES to you — the threat in prose, not a number (the number comes from tier). Folded into the encounter seed so the GM knows how it hurts.

pressures.description: which crafts answer it — the mechanics the encounter frame runs (e.g. 'KNOW (sense which are real)', 'WARD (shield the eyes)'). An empty list is the hollow-monster case: a scary description with nothing the player's crafts can engage.

clean.description: how it dies / what it leaves. Authored on all 26 roster entries but read by NO consumer today — optional, and not part of the born-whole contract.

habitat.description: SNG-661 §3.1: the place tags this creature belongs to — terrain (marsh, river, mountain, ruin, underplace, cold…) and its people's own lands (ashwarden, rootkin, mason…). ⛔ READ AS THE ENCOUNTER'S `tags`, so a grue only rises where a place is dark and a siren only sings where there is water. Absent means eligible everywhere, which is what all 28 of the first roster do.

storiedBy.description: SNG-661: whose folklore made it real when the Storm came through. ⛑ Also decides who knows its `storyRule` from the first look — a character of that people grew up on the tale. `(every people)` / `(many peoples)` means common ground, known to all.

storyRule.description: SNG-661 §3.2: the folk remedy from the tale, AND IT IS TRUE — a lit passage stops the grue, a mirror stops the basilisk, running water stops hellhounds. The GM is given it only once the character knows it (their own people's tale, or a KNOW success against the thing) and is told that it really works.

unique.description: one in the world (the phoenix, the kraken, the Wakeful Beast). Never offered by a random table.

affinity.description: the pole or element the thing belongs to — display and lore.

hasSelf.description: whether there is somebody in there — read by the class table so a craft that requires a SELF has something to be answered by (CCODE-315). ⚠️ Undeclared until SNG-661 although 41 of the staged creatures set it: found by reading the schema against the staged file rather than against the list of what was thought to be new.
